newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Chirac to persuade US on Romania in NATO.
newsitem.headline: Chirac to persuade US on Romania in NATO.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac vowed on Saturday to try to persuade the United States to accept the admission of Romania to an expanded NATO in addition to three favoured ex-communist states.

Chirac told a news conference after a two-day visit to Romania that the United States was the main obstacle to extending membership to Romania and possibly Slovenia. Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are viewed as near-certain entrants to be announced at a NATO summit in July.
"This enlargement presupposes that beyond the three countries due to enter NATO -- Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary -- a fourth and, possibly, a fifth should also be admitted," he said.
"France will do everything possible to persuade our partners in the Atlantic alliance to ensure Romania's admission to NATO from the Madrid summit in July."

He discounted a suggestion from a Romanian journalist that Germany was most reluctant to take in Romania. "You spoke about Germany. It is not there that the biggest difficulty lies. What we must do is to persuade the United States to accept this."

In an address to Romania's parliament on Friday, Chirac cited Slovenia as a possible fifth entrant in the first wave of admissions. At the news conference, he repeated that expansion "in good conditions" was linked to prior conclusion of an accord between NATO and Russia.
